facts.fact: The page states that 58% of consumers are already using voice search to find local business information.
facts.quote: A massive 58% of consumers are already using voice search to find local business information.

facts.fact: The page states that 76% of people who own smart speakers perform local searches every week.
facts.quote: for those who own smart speakers, it's a weekly habit, 76% of them perform local searches every single week.

facts.fact: The page states that nearly half of all voice searches have local intent.
facts.quote: Despite nearly half of all voice searches having local intent, a shockingly small 4% of businesses are set up to be found this way.

facts.fact: The page states that only 4% of businesses are set up to be found through voice search.
facts.quote: a shockingly small 4% of businesses are set up to be found this way.

facts.fact: The article states that a business's Name, Address, and Phone number (NAP) needs to be 100% identical everywhere online.
facts.quote: It needs to be **100% identical** everywhere online.

facts.fact: The article says the NAP must be exactly the same on the business website, its Google Business Profile, and major directories such as Yelp, Apple Maps, and Bing Places.
facts.quote: Your NAP must be exactly the same on your website, your GBP, and on major directories like Yelp, Apple Maps, and Bing Places.

facts.fact: The article says several free tools can implement schema markup without coding, including Google's Rich Results Test and Merkle's Schema Markup Generator.
facts.quote: several free tools have made this a simple, fill-in-the-blanks process. Google’s own [Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and generators like **Merkle’s Schema Markup Generator**

facts.fact: The article lists Price Range as one of the core details LocalBusiness schema helps define, illustrated with the notation $, $$, $$$.
facts.quote: **Price Range:** A general idea of your pricing (e.g., $, $$, $$$).

facts.fact: The article states that LocalBusiness schema is the gold standard for any physical business and covers business name, address, phone number, opening hours, aggregate rating, and price range.
facts.quote: For any physical business, the gold standard is **LocalBusiness schema**.

facts.fact: Adwave states that local businesses can generally expect real, tangible results from voice search optimization within 3 to 6 months.
facts.quote: Generally, you can expect to see real, tangible results from your **voice search optimization for local businesses** within **3 to 6 months**.

facts.fact: Adwave says foundational work such as cleaning up a Google Business Profile and NAP consistency can show results faster, and that it has seen businesses get more calls in just a few weeks from these fixes.
facts.quote: I’ve seen businesses get more calls in just a few weeks from these high-impact fixes alone.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its platform runs local TV advertising campaigns on ESPN, NBC, and other popular channels.
facts.quote: By running campaigns on major platforms like ESPN, NBC, and other popular channels, you build widespread awareness right in your service area.
